hero.slogan: Created by people. For the community.
hero.valueLine: Community participates in the value created by the network.
hero.lead: Built by the community. Shared by the community. Ordinary people take part in issuance, network-fee routing, and Growth referral — while dedicated validators secure consensus. Participants are not validators.
hero.unlike: On a typical blockchain, users mostly pay fees. Here, community participation is designed into the economy.

value.title: Three distinct ways the community takes part
value.subtitle: Token issuance, network fees, and Growth referral are three separate mechanisms. They are never merged into one personal payout.

cards.title: 10% of every new token goes to the community pool
cards.body: Every standard token launched through the network sends 10% of its initial supply to that token’s Community Pool — then to the community. Not a personal payout, and not 10% of every fee.

cards.title: Fees don’t disappear — they are routed
cards.body: Eligible network fees follow the protocol fee split. This is network-economy routing, not a promise that every participant is paid from every fee.

cards.title: L1 70% · L2 30% of the Growth reward budget
cards.body: Growth Pool (15% of eligible fees) funds two paid referral lines: L1 at 70% and L2 at 30% of the Growth reward budget. Distinct from Token Factory supply and from the network fee split.

partner.title: You → L1 → L2
partner.subtitle: Active Beta Growth payout: L1 70% · L2 30% of the Growth reward budget. Growth Pool is 15% of eligible fees. Distinct from network fee destinations and from the 10% of each new token that goes to the community pool.
partner.budgetNote: Percentages are shares of the Growth reward budget after 15% of each protocol fee goes to the Growth Pool — not shares of every network fee.

details.title: Two paid lines
details.body: L1 (direct referral) receives 70% and L2 (second level) receives 30% of the active Growth reward budget.

details.title: Separate from fees and tokens
details.body: L1/L2 Growth weights are not the network fee split and not the 10% of each new token for the community pool. Growth Pool receives 15% of each protocol fee with its own settlement rules.

details.title: This site
details.body: There is no referral login or dashboard on this public website. Growth referral lives with network participation.

join.title: How to participate
join.subtitle: Join People’s Blockchain as a community participant — from a phone, tablet, or browser.

steps.title: Start here
steps.body: Use a phone, tablet, or browser. You join as a participant — not as a consensus validator.

steps.title: Create a non-custodial wallet
steps.body: Generate a 12-word phrase in the browser and encrypt it with a password, or sign in with Google for a synced wallet. With the 12-word wallet, keys never leave this device.

steps.title: See assets on the explorer
steps.body: Look up blocks, transactions, addresses, tokens, and NFTs on the public scanner.

steps.title: Take part in the economy
steps.body: Pay Token Factory and NFT mint fees from the same wallet. The 10% community-pool share on new tokens, network fees, and Growth referral stay three separate mechanisms.

whatIs.title: What is People's Blockchain?
whatIs.summary: People's Blockchain is community infrastructure: ordinary devices for participation, protocol-level creation of tokens and projects, and Proof-of-Stake validators for block production. Participants are not validators.

items.title: Consensus
items.summary: PoS validators propose and attest blocks. Mobile participation never votes in quorum.

items.title: Economics
items.summary: Eligible network fees follow the protocol fee split. User-token markets are a separate pipeline.

items.title: Participation
items.summary: Phones, tablets, and browsers. Participants are not validators.

items.title: Technology
items.summary: Integer-safe multi-asset ledger, a peer network, and tools to explore the chain.

flow.title: How it works
flow.subtitle: One path through the network. Open a step for the exact mechanic.

steps.title: USER
steps.summary: A person with a wallet on a phone, tablet, or browser.
steps.detail: Start with a non-custodial account on a phone, tablet, or browser. You join as a person in the community — not as a validator.

steps.title: TRANSACTION
steps.summary: Transfers, launches, curve trades, and other signed operations.
steps.detail: Eligible operations pay a protocol fee in PPL. Every action is signed and checked before it is accepted.

steps.title: VALIDATOR
steps.summary: Stake-backed nodes that propose and attest.
steps.detail: Validators are dedicated infrastructure. Phones and browsers do not produce blocks.

steps.title: BLOCK
steps.detail: Validators assemble signed operations into blocks. Everyday devices do not sit in that process.

steps.title: NETWORK
steps.detail: Validator nodes share blocks with each other so the network stays in one state.

steps.title: COMMUNITY
steps.summary: Network fees and each token's community share stay in separate pipelines.
steps.detail: Every protocol fee is split: 30% to validators, 25% to the community pool, 20% to the treasury, 10% to liquidity, 15% to Growth, 0% burned — including fractional fees. Standard user-created tokens send 10% of that token's supply to its own community pool — that is not a network fee.

ppl.title: People (PPL)
ppl.summary: People is the native asset of People's Blockchain. Ticker: PPL.

cards.title: UTILITY
cards.body: Settlement asset for network operations: fees, token creation, and protocol services described in the specs.

cards.title: NETWORK
cards.body: Denominates eligible protocol fees that the live fee splitter routes with the 30/25/20/10/15/0 split.

cards.title: FEES
cards.body: Paid in PPL on eligible operations. Exact fee schedules remain protocol/config — this page does not invent rates.

cards.title: PARTICIPATION
cards.body: Used in network-economy accounting. Participation Power is not a transferable token and is not validator voting power.

ppl.notMarket: This site does not publish price, market cap, listings, ROI, APY, liquidity depth, or future price.

network.title: Network & validators
network.summary: Consensus is Proof-of-Stake with a leader and an attestation quorum. Phones are participants, not validators.

facts.label: Role

facts.value: Public testnet v2 is running. This is not Mainnet.

economics.title: Network fee economics
economics.summary: Every protocol fee is split: 30% to validators, 25% to the community pool, 20% to the treasury, 10% to liquidity, 15% to Growth, 0% burned — including fractional fees.
economics.growthNote: Growth Pool receives 15% of eligible fees. It is not guaranteed income, not a passive return, and not an investment product.
economics.detailsBody: Every protocol fee is split: 30% to validators, 25% to the community pool, 20% to the treasury, 10% to liquidity, 15% to Growth, 0% burned — including fractional fees. After whole-number division, any remainder stays with validators. The 10% of each new token that goes to the community pool is a different path — not a network fee.

tokenMarket.title: Create → Launch → Project feed → Trade
tokenMarket.subtitle: Create a token, launch it with built-in pricing, let others find it, and trade on the launch curve.

steps.title: Create
steps.body: Use the Token Factory form: image, name, ticker, supply, then pay in PPL.

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: A virtual bonding curve provides continuous pricing from the first block.

steps.title: Project feed
steps.body: Projects appear in the public feed so communities can find them.

steps.title: Trade
steps.body: Buy and sell on the launch curve, then swap in the live token/PPL AMM pool.

expandItems: Launch pricing uses a constant-product curve with exact integer math.
A protocol trading fee on the curve is routed through network fee economics.
Standard launch split includes a mandatory 10% of that token's supply to its own community pool (not a PPL network fee).
Creator vesting keeps most of the creator's share unlocking over time, so the community is not dumped on day one.
